questionStem: Someone says: “Rural labor is shrinking, so agriculture is weakening.” Build a reply from what the source actually shows.

templates.text: The source shows that [shown], but that does not tell us [missing].

choices.text: the share of workers in this sector fell
whether the number of workers or the output fell
a smaller share alone does not show it is weaker

feedback.text: The source shows a falling share. It does not say whether the number of workers or output fell, so the claim goes beyond the data.

challengeCandidates.label: TN1
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the reply starts from the number of workers
challengeCandidates.message: Does Table 8.1 give the number of workers, or their share?

challengeCandidates.label: TN2
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the reply uses the first template
challengeCandidates.message: What else would you need to know before saying that agriculture is weaker?

challengeCandidates.label: TN3
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the reply says something the source does not show
challengeCandidates.message: Which sentence in the source supports the part you filled in?

challengeCandidates.label: TN4
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the reply uses the second template
challengeCandidates.message: A large share today: does that answer the claim about weakening?

challengeCandidates.label: Fallback
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When none of the above applies
challengeCandidates.message: Read your reply again. Does each part come from what the source shows?
